newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* The Dow Jones industrials average fell 41.64 points.
* PepsiCo Inc plans to create a separate bottling division. Meanwhile, Coca-Cola Co confirmed that it's trying to banish Dr Pepper/Seven Up from McDonald's restaurants.
* Chrysler Corp said its sales of cars and trucks fell 16.6 percent in May.
* Seagate Technology Inc said its fourth quarter earnings are likely to fall below expectations because of weak demand for computer disk drives.
* Enron Corp said it has agreed to pay $440 million to settle a dispute with Phillips Petroleum Co.
* The computer software business has increased 12.5 percent to become the United States' third-largest manufacturing industry, according to an industry-sponsored study.
* Smith Barney has dismissed its New England regional director, whose role in raising campaign cash for his brother, U.S. Rep. James H. Maloney, D-Connecticut, is under investigation.
* Czech Republican Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus admits he made mistakes as he ushered the country from Communism to capitalism.
* A federal judge has issued statistical guidelines as a way to limit jury awards for "pain and suffering" in civil cases.
* Analysts believe Lehman Brothers is interested in joining the parade of marriages between brokerage firms.

* An employee for Bear Stearns Cos Inc has said an executive at the firm told him to destroy documents sought as part of an investigation into its relationship with the defunct A.R. Baron & Co, according to paperwork between lawyers in the case.
* Although statistics showed slower spending in May among consumers, the month brought unexpected strength in manufacturing spending.
* The U.S. dollar rose amid concerns that the Euro would be weakened by the Socialist victory in France and the dispute between the German government and the central bank.
